frontier.hypothesis: func_800747D8 is byte-complete in pure C at V3's spelling; the only thing between it and COMPLETED-C is moving ownership of jtbl_80015A0C from the hand-transcribed array to real compiler output, which the isolated sandbox can never score.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 emits a switch's ADDR_VEC into the .rodata of the TU containing the switch. bb2.ld orders text1a_b_pre_rodata.o, text1b.o, text1a_b_mid_rodata.o, and text1b.o already owns jtbl_80015988 at 0x80015988, so text1b.o's single .rodata cannot straddle the 0x800159A0..0x80015A0B run that text1a_b_mid_rodata.o supplies. bb2.ld is outside every grind session's allowed surface, so the fix must stay inside the C files.
frontier.next_probe: In a session whose scope covers src/text1b.c AND src/text1a_b_mid_rodata.c: declare `const char D_800159A0[16]`, `const u32 jtbl_800159B0[8]` and `const u32 jtbl_800159D0[15]` in src/text1b.c between func_8006B578 and func_800747D8 (GCC emits .rodata in declaration order), delete those three plus jtbl_80015A0C from src/text1a_b_mid_rodata.c, apply candidate.c, and verify with the FULL build (`& tools/wteng.ps1 main build`) against SHA1 62efab4f73f992798c43e8c730aa43baa10bb4fa - the sandbox score will stay at 2 either way and is not the right instrument here.

frontier.hypothesis: V3's duplicated `sound = 4;` can be replaced by a single-assignment spelling that still puts a CODE_LABEL between the assignment and the test, which would remove the need to claim the duplicated-statement-into-arms family at all.
frontier.mechanism: The gate is purely tools/gcc-2.7.2/rtlanal.c:886-888's CODE_LABEL stop feeding tools/gcc-2.7.2/jump.c:1178. Any control-flow shape in which the assignment is executed before a label that the test's block begins with satisfies it; V4 proved that a `break`-converged switch puts the label on the wrong side, but other shapes (e.g. a single arm assigning and the other arm reaching the block by a goto that skips the assignment, or an enclosing if that guards only the assignment) have not been enumerated.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate single-assignment control-flow shapes for the case-1/case-2 -> selection_sound path with tools/spelling_enum.py + sweep_variants.py (the s4 tool pair), scoring each with `sandbox --disable all`, and keep any that reaches 2/208 with one textual `sound = 4;`. If none exists, the duplicated-statement-into-arms citation is unavoidable and the next session should write self_vet.md against .claude/rules/duplicated-statement-into-arms.md with a /* FAKE */ annotation naming jump.c:1178 / rtlanal.c:886-888 as the mechanism.

frontier.hypothesis: The V1 route (a second real statement duplicated into both arms of the original if/else, blocking jump.c:754-860 via its multi-insn-arm predicates) reaches the same 2/208 and may be classifiable under a different, easier family than V3's.
frontier.mechanism: tools/gcc-2.7.2/jump.c:775 and tools/gcc-2.7.2/jump.c:784-789 both require single-insn arms; two-insn arms defeat the normalisation and, transitively, the store-flag block's `reallabelprev == temp` test at tools/gcc-2.7.2/jump.c:1066.
frontier.next_probe: Re-measure memory/grind/func_800747D8/vol-dup-arms-floor2.c and take its --diff to confirm it too has zero source-level hunks; then compare the two forms' cheat-checklist exposure (V1 invents a `vol` local whose only purpose is to be duplicated - likely worse under T1/T6 than V3's duplicated real default) before deciding which body a submission session should carry.
